AGRICULTURE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #5
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Why do we sprinkle soil or old compost between layers? (1 mark)
   A. It adds tiny living things that help wastes to rot
   B. It makes the heap sweeter
   C. It keeps birds away
   D. It adds plastic

2. What is the purpose of sticks at the bottom of the compost heap? (1 mark)
   A. They keep the heap dry forever
   B. They add plant food
   C. They make it look neat
   D. They let air move through the heap

3. Which is a benefit of compost to sandy soil? (1 mark)
   A. It makes the soil disappear
   B. It makes the soil more sandy
   C. It helps the soil to hold water
   D. It removes all nutrients

4. After about how long should the compost heap first be turned? (1 mark)
   A. One year
   B. One hour
   C. Never
   D. Two to three weeks

5. Why should the drip container be covered? (1 mark)
   A. To warm the water
   B. To keep out leaves and mosquitoes
   C. To increase evaporation
   D. To make water sweet

6. What should you do if a hole in a drip pipe is blocked? (1 mark)
   A. Throw away the whole system
   B. Cut the pipe in half
   C. Clear it gently with a thin wire
   D. Pour hot oil in it

7. Why does a higher container give a faster drip? (1 mark)
   A. It has a lid
   B. It is nearer the sun
   C. Gravity pushes the water more strongly
   D. It has more air

8. What is the best time of day to water crops? (1 mark)
   A. Never
   B. Noon
   C. Midnight only
   D. Early morning or late afternoon

9. Which fuel comes in a metal cylinder? (1 mark)
   A. Firewood
   B. Gas
   C. Charcoal
   D. Dung cakes

10. Why do we soak dry beans before cooking? (1 mark)
   A. They dry out
   B. They become bigger than the pot
   C. They cook in less time so less fuel is used
   D. They become poisonous

11. Why should food be cut into small pieces before cooking? (1 mark)
   A. They burn the pot
   B. Small pieces cook faster and use less fuel
   C. They need more water
   D. They take longer to cook

12. What is the danger of burning charcoal in a closed room? (1 mark)
   A. It makes the room too cold
   B. It gives off a poisonous gas
   C. It creates rain
   D. It makes the walls bigger

13. Where is a scarecrow best placed? (1 mark)
   A. Inside the house
   B. At the river
   C. In the middle or at the side of the crop where animals come from
   D. Far from the crop

14. Why is poison a bad way to deal with wild animals? (1 mark)
   A. It makes crops grow
   B. It is too slow to spread
   C. It can also kill other animals and people
   D. It is too cheap

15. Why should a seedbed for tiny seeds be fine? (1 mark)
   A. It is a school rule
   B. Fine soil makes seeds bigger
   C. Lumps help seeds
   D. Tiny seeds cannot push through big lumps

16. Why do we weed around fruit plants? (1 mark)
   A. Weeds add sugar
   B. Weeds take water and food from the plants
   C. Weeds protect the stem
   D. Weeds give fruits

17. Which nutrient in oranges and guavas helps the body to heal cuts and fight colds? (1 mark)
   A. Cooking oil
   B. Salt
   C. Vitamin C
   D. Starch

18. Which sign shows that a guava is ripe? (1 mark)
   A. It is dry and black
   B. It turns yellowish and smells sweet
   C. It has flowers on it
   D. It is dark green and hard

19. Where should the graft joint of a grafted seedling be? (1 mark)
   A. Deep below the soil
   B. Above the ground
   C. In water
   D. In the compost

20. Which of these is a sign of a healthy young fruit plant? (1 mark)
   A. Rotten stem
   B. Fallen stem
   C. Yellow and dry leaves
   D. Green leaves and steady growth

21. Which is a way of protecting ripe fruit from birds and monkeys? (1 mark)
   A. Cut the tree
   B. Cover trees with nets or use scare methods
   C. Poison the animals
   D. Leave them ripe for months

22. What is the meat from cattle called? (1 mark)
   A. Beef
   B. Pork
   C. Chicken
   D. Mutton

23. Why should raw milk be boiled before drinking? (1 mark)
   A. To make it thicker
   B. To kill germs
   C. To make it colder
   D. To make it blue

24. What is the young one of a sheep called? (1 mark)
   A. Calf
   B. Lamb
   C. Foal
   D. Kid

25. Why is a food journal kept for a week? (1 mark)
   A. To find cheap shops
   B. To count the number of plates
   C. To check whether meals are balanced
   D. To improve handwriting only

26. Which of these root foods gives the body energy? (1 mark)
   A. Egg
   B. Milk
   C. Kale
   D. Sweet potato

27. Why should vegetables be boiled for a short time only? (1 mark)
   A. Long boiling destroys some vitamins
   B. It saves nothing
   C. Short boiling makes them poisonous
   D. Long boiling makes them colder

28. Which of these is used for boiling food? (1 mark)
   A. A plate
   B. A frying pan only
   C. A basket
   D. A saucepan with a lid

29. Why do farmers and cleaners wear personal protective equipment? (1 mark)
   A. To protect the body from dirt, injury and germs
   B. To make work slower
   C. To look tall
   D. To keep food hot

30. What should you do after coughing into your hands? (1 mark)
   A. Wipe them on your clothes
   B. Ignore it
   C. Shake hands
   D. Wash your hands with soap and water

31. Which part is often forgotten when washing hands? (1 mark)
   A. The elbows only
   B. The knees
   C. Only the palms
   D. Under the nails and between the fingers

32. How can a dustpan be improvised? (1 mark)
   A. Use a rope
   B. Use a chair
   C. Cut a jerrican or flat tin
   D. Use a sack

33. What is refuse? (1 mark)
   A. Rubbish or waste
   B. Food
   C. Clean water
   D. Soap

34. How should broken glass be disposed of? (1 mark)
   A. Left on the floor
   B. Thrown in the yard
   C. Wrapped in thick paper and given to an adult
   D. Put in the compost

35. Where should clean PPE be stored? (1 mark)
   A. In a wet corner
   B. On the floor
   C. In a dry, clean place
   D. In a dirty box

36. Which PPE protects the hands? (1 mark)
   A. Gloves
   B. Gumboots
   C. Headgear
   D. Dust mask

37. Which PPE protects the head from sun and dust? (1 mark)
   A. Dust mask
   B. Gloves
   C. Headgear
   D. Gumboots

38. Which of these is another tacking stitch? (1 mark)
   A. French knot
   B. Long and short tacking
   C. Blanket stitch
   D. Herringbone

39. How should you carry scissors? (1 mark)
   A. By the blades
   B. With the points held down
   C. With the points up
   D. Running

40. About how long is the long stitch in long and short tacking? (1 mark)
   A. 2 cm
   B. 2 mm
   C. 2 metres
   D. 20 cm

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Give two disadvantages of shallow frying. (2 marks)

42. Prepare a balanced menu for one day for a Grade 4 child using local foods and explain why it is balanced. (5 marks)

43. Explain why a scarecrow becomes less useful if it is never moved. (3 marks)

44. What should you do after cooking to keep the kitchen safe and clean? (2 marks)

45. Name two materials that can be used to make compost. (2 marks)

46. Why do we dust before sweeping? (2 marks)

47. Describe how to build a compost heap using layers. (4 marks)

48. Give two ways of protecting fruits from birds and monkeys without killing them. (2 marks)

49. Explain four things that may happen to a child who does not eat a balanced diet. (4 marks)

50. Why should plastic not be burnt? (2 marks)

51. Name two problems that can attack ripe fruits. (2 marks)

52. Why do we need protective foods? (2 marks)

53. Describe how to make a simple trellis for passion fruit. (4 marks)

54. Give three ways of disposing of refuse safely. (3 marks)

55. How do fruits help our health? (3 marks)

56. Compare a watering can with drip irrigation. (4 marks)

57. Give two reasons why soil should be conserved. (2 marks)

58. Why should an adult make the holes in the pipe? (2 marks)

59. Describe how to make a scarecrow. (4 marks)

60. Describe how to make a handkerchief hem using tacking. (4 marks)

61. Why should personal items like towels not be shared? (2 marks)
pages.answers:
AGRICULTURE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #5 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — It adds tiny living things that help wastes to rot
   Soil and old compost carry bacteria and fungi that break down wastes.

2. D — They let air move through the heap
   Air helps the tiny living things rot the wastes.

3. C — It helps the soil to hold water
   Compost holds water like a sponge.

4. D — Two to three weeks
   Turning after a few weeks gives air and mixes the heap.

5. B — To keep out leaves and mosquitoes
   A cover keeps water clean and stops mosquitoes breeding.

6. C — Clear it gently with a thin wire
   A thin wire clears blockages without damaging the pipe.

7. C — Gravity pushes the water more strongly
   A higher container gives a bigger push for water flowing down.

8. D — Early morning or late afternoon
   The sun is less hot, so less water evaporates.

9. B — Gas
   LPG gas is stored under pressure in a cylinder.

10. C — They cook in less time so less fuel is used
   Soaked beans soften and cook faster.

11. B — Small pieces cook faster and use less fuel
   Small pieces heat through quickly.

12. B — It gives off a poisonous gas
   Charcoal fumes can make people ill or worse.

13. C — In the middle or at the side of the crop where animals come from
   It must be seen by the animals that come to the crop.

14. C — It can also kill other animals and people
   Poison harms living things that are not the target.

15. D — Tiny seeds cannot push through big lumps
   Tiny seeds have little food and are weak.

16. B — Weeds take water and food from the plants
   Weeds compete with the crop.

17. C — Vitamin C
   Vitamin C helps the body fight illness.

18. B — It turns yellowish and smells sweet
   Ripe guavas change colour and smell sweet.

19. B — Above the ground
   Buried joints can rot or grow roots of the wrong kind.

20. D — Green leaves and steady growth
   Healthy plants grow green.

21. B — Cover trees with nets or use scare methods
   Peaceful protection.

22. A — Beef
   Beef comes from cattle.

23. B — To kill germs
   Boiling makes it safe.

24. B — Lamb
   A young sheep is a lamb.

25. C — To check whether meals are balanced
   A journal shows patterns in eating.

26. D — Sweet potato
   Sweet potatoes are starchy.

27. A — Long boiling destroys some vitamins
   Vitamins are lost with too much cooking.

28. D — A saucepan with a lid
   A saucepan holds water.

29. A — To protect the body from dirt, injury and germs
   PPE is clothing and gear that protects us from harm.

30. D — Wash your hands with soap and water
   Germs from coughs stay on hands.

31. D — Under the nails and between the fingers
   Germs hide there.

32. C — Cut a jerrican or flat tin
   A cut jerrican forms a scoop.

33. A — Rubbish or waste
   Refuse means waste.

34. C — Wrapped in thick paper and given to an adult
   This prevents cuts.

35. C — In a dry, clean place
   Damp PPE grows mould.

36. A — Gloves
   Gloves cover the hands.

37. C — Headgear
   Hats, caps and scarves cover the head.

38. B — Long and short tacking
   Long and short tacking is another type.

39. B — With the points held down
   This avoids injury.

40. A — 2 cm
   The long stitch is about 2 cm.

SECTION B
----
41. (2 marks)
   Answer: It can splash and burn, and too much oil is not good for health.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each disadvantage.

42. (5 marks)
   Answer: Breakfast: porridge and egg; lunch: ugali, beans and sukuma wiki; supper: rice, fish and cabbage with fruit. It includes energy, body-building and protective foods in every day.
   Working / marking points: 3 marks for a menu with all groups, 2 marks for correct explanation.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: Birds and animals soon notice it never moves, learn that it is harmless, and come back to eat the crops.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for noticing, 1 mark for learning it is harmless, 1 mark for returning to the crops.

44. (2 marks)
   Answer: Put out the fire or switch off the gas, wash and store utensils and wipe the working area.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for fire or gas, 1 mark for cleaning.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: Vegetable peelings, dry leaves, grass, straw or animal dung (any two).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct material.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: Dust falls to the floor, so sweeping afterwards removes it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for dust falls, 1 mark for sweeping removes.

47. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose a shady place; lay sticks; add a dry layer, a green layer and dung; sprinkle soil and water; repeat to chest height; cover the heap.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for place, base and layers, soil and water, and covering.

48. (2 marks)
   Answer: Cover with nets, use scarecrows, noise or shiny objects (any two).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

49. (4 marks)
   Answer: Weakness, tiredness, frequent illness, slow growth, poor concentration (any four).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

50. (2 marks)
   Answer: The smoke is harmful to health and the environment.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for harmful smoke, 1 mark for the environment or health.

51. (2 marks)
   Answer: Fruit flies, birds or monkeys (any two).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

52. (2 marks)
   Answer: They give vitamins and minerals that fight sickness and keep the body healthy.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for fight sickness, 1 mark for vitamins or minerals.

53. (4 marks)
   Answer: Fix strong posts about 2 m tall; tie strong wires or strings between them; plant seedlings near the posts; tie the stems gently to the wires.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct step.

54. (3 marks)
   Answer: Compost organic waste; put other waste in a bin with a lid and take it to a collection point; reuse or recycle paper, plastic and glass; wrap broken glass.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way.

55. (3 marks)
   Answer: They give vitamins that fight illness, fibre that helps digestion and water that keeps the body healthy.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

56. (4 marks)
   Answer: A watering can wets a wide area and much water is lost by running off and by evaporation. Drip irrigation puts water beside the roots slowly, so less is used, fewer weeds grow, and the leaves stay dry.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for the watering can, 2 marks for drip irrigation.

57. (2 marks)
   Answer: Soil grows our food, and if it is washed away or made poor the crops will fail.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for soil grows food, 1 mark for erosion or loss of plant food.

58. (2 marks)
   Answer: Nails and awls are sharp and can hurt children.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for sharp tools, 1 mark for safety or injuries.

59. (4 marks)
   Answer: Fix a long pole firmly in the ground; tie a shorter stick across it; put a stuffed head on top; dress with a stuffed shirt and hat; add tins or shiny strips.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four correct steps.

60. (4 marks)
   Answer: Cut a 25 cm square; fold each edge twice by about 1 cm; pin; tack along the fold with even tacking; check evenness; sew permanently and remove tacking.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four steps.

61. (2 marks)
   Answer: Germs and skin infections spread through them.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for germs, 1 mark for infection.
